subject: [PATCH v7 0/5] mm/page_counter: move stock from mem_cgroup to page_counter

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Michal Hocko noted that the patch description initially seemed to imply an 'opt-in' mechanism for page_counters, but clarified that this was not the case and only referred to the memory page_counter and memsw page_counter for cgroup v2. He expressed understanding after reading the original cover letter again.

Reviewer Michal Hocko asked how the patch handles limiting the cache to leaf memcgroups, expressing relief that it addresses one of his concerns.

Reviewer Michal Hocko expressed initial concerns about the patch, but after clarification that it's a 'leaf only' feature, he found it more understandable and acknowledged the benefits of caching on all levels of the hierarchy.

Reviewer Michal Hocko questioned the necessity of adding caching for memsw charges, suggesting that disabling it would be a simpler solution if opt-in is available.
reviews.raw_body:
OK, that makes it clear to me now.

[...]

---

limiting cache to leaf memcgs makes a lot of sense and addresses a big
concern I had. How exactly does this work?

---

Yes, these are all good arguments. Especially when clarified that this
leaf only feature. I have to say I was struggling to see how caching on
all levels of the hierarchy would work in practice.

---

Right but is there any actual point in adding caching for memsw charges
now? If you have a way to opt-in to caching then you can simply disabled
that for memsw counter altogether. Fewer problems to deal with, explain
etc...

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary:
Author addressed Michal's concern about the 'opt-in' wording in the patch, explaining it was meant for memory page_counter and memsw page_counter, and agreed to change the wording in the next version.

Author addresses Michal's concern about the patch's scope and potential optimizations, agrees to add leaf-only caching to the current series to maintain parity with existing code.

The author acknowledges that removing stocking for memsw exacerbates the issue of invariant memory <= memsw being broken, and proposes removing stocking for cgroup v1 users as a potential solution.
reviews.raw_body:
It's not a big change, actually. This was the implementation from the
origianl RFC of the series:

https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260410210742.550489-8-joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com/

The idea is that you treat a cgroup as a leaf until it becomes a parent,
at which point you drain the stock. Stock can land on the parent due
to hierarchy walks, but I can also write another part to this that
prevents stock from getting cached when a cgroup has children.

---

Sounds good. If it makes sense to you then, I can fold in the
leaf-only caching into this series to maintain more parity with the
existing code. How does that sound?

---

I think the problem actually still exists, unfortunately. In fact I
think the issue becomes bigger if you remove stocking for memsw.

Let's say only memory gets stock. Then on a single page charge for a
new cgroup:

memory page_counter charges 64 pages to refill the stock, memsw only
charges 1 page to fulfill the current allocation. Then you have
memory: 64 pages
memsw: 1 page

And the invariant that memory <= memsw is immediately broken.

Unfortunately only stocking for memsw is not a solution as well since
successful memsw charges still charge memory and will therefore go
through a hierarchy walk.

Actually maybe then, the solution is just to remove stocking for
cgroup v1 users? Does that sound like a fair tradeoff to you?

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that caching memsw through the charging path breaks the invariant that memory <= memsw, and suggested removing stocking for cgroup v1 users as a potential solution.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, you are right. We do actually cache memsw through the charging path
which charges both mem and memsw with the batch. 
-- 
Michal Hocko
SUSE Labs

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges Michal's concern about cgroup v1 implications for fuzziness and explains that the patch only changes 'why' and 'when' stocking becomes fuzzy, not the userspace POV.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks, Michal! So it seems like we are in alignment on everything
except the cgroup v1 implications for fuzziness. FWIW I think nothing
really changes from the userspace POV. memsw and memory usage has
always been fuzzy due to stocking, so all this series does is to
change "why" and "when" the stocking becomes fuzzy.

What do you think about this? The other alternative would be to remove
stocking for cgroup v1 users completely. But I am not sure that is a
good solution either. For the record, I tried making the stock tied
together so that they refill together, but that was a nightmare in
terms of added complexity.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch doesn't fundamentally change the cgroup v1 implications for fuzziness, and suggested considering removing stocking for cgroup v1 users completely as an alternative solution.

Reviewer argued that removing stocking for cgroup v1 users would be overreaching and cripple performance without sufficient added value, suggesting a more nuanced approach is needed.
reviews.raw_body:
Right. The discrepancy was not so obvious but I agree that this change
doesn't fundamentally change the picture.

---

Nah, that seems overreaching without much added value. While we do not
support new features in v1 we shouldn't cripple performance for those
users unless there is no other way around.

-- 
Michal Hocko
SUSE Labs

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged Michal's concern about cgroup v1 implications and agreed that nothing changes from the userspace POV, confirming alignment on all issues except fuzziness.
reviews.raw_body:
Sounds good with me, and I also agree here. OK! I think it seems like
we are in alignment with everything. Let me spin up a new cover letter
being more explicit about everything we've covered here and send it
out soon. This was really helpful for me, thank you for your time
Michal : -)

Have a great day!!
Joshua

2026-11-02.patch_summary: This patch series moves the concept of 'stock' from mem_cgroup to page_counter, which changes how and when memory stocking becomes fuzzy for cgroup v1 users. The change aims to simplify the logic behind stocking, but may introduce complexity in certain scenarios.
